topics.label: Course Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, the cancer lecture series, and the specific learning outcomes for the session.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Endogenous Factors, Environmental Risks, and Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental causes of cancer, contrasting endogenous random mutations and 'bad luck' with environmental exposures and global epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Infectious Agents in Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how biological pathogens promote malignancy, featuring a detailed case study of Burkitt lymphoma and its co-factors.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mutagens: Mechanisms of DNA Damage and Metabolic Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how specific chemical compounds and physical radiation undergo metabolic processing to form DNA adducts, mutations, and oxidative damage.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Tissue Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine non-mutagenic mechanisms of carcinogenesis, distinguishing tumor promoters and inflammatory microenvironments from initiators and explaining tissue- and developmental-stage vulnerabilities.

topics.label: Methods for Detecting and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the scientific methodologies used to establish carcinogenicity—including mutational signatures, epidemiology, animal models, and the Ames test—and conclude with risk-benefit considerations.
